name: Tho
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Nguyễn Hữu Hoành, Bùi Thị Ngọc Anh & Hoàng Ngọc Tuệ. 2022. A Cuoi Language Description and Extensive Glossary. JSEALS Special Publication 10. Honolulu: University of Hawai'i Press. 122 pp. http://hdl.handle.net/10524/52504
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Silent on stress. Section 3 'Phonological summary' (pp. 4-10, Tan Hop Cuoi) covers syllable structure C1(C2)V(C3)+T, onsets, vowels, codas and five tones (35, 53, 24, 31ʔ, 44ʔ); the words 'stress', 'accent', 'prominence' do not occur anywhere in the 128-page PDF (only 'phrasal intonation' once, in the syntax chapter, p. 21); no stress marks in any transcription. Describes Cuoi as 'an isolating and monosyllabic language' in which 'syllables.. are both morphemes and single words' (p. 4).

sources.citation: Nguyễn Hữu Hoành & Nguyễn Văn Lợi. 2019. Tones in the Cuoi Language of Tan Ki District in Nghe An Province, Vietnam. Journal of the Southeast Asian Linguistics Society 12(1): lvii-lxvi. http://hdl.handle.net/10524/52449
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Silent on stress. Acoustic/phonological description of the Tan Hop (Tan Ky) tone system: seven surface tones (five on sonorant-final syllables, two on stopped syllables), analysable as five phonological tones; states 'Cuoi is a monosyllabic language, having only monosyllabic roots, not sesquisyllabic roots' (p. lvii). No mention of stress, accent or prominence.

sources.citation: Ferlus, Michel. 2001 [English version]. Hypercorrections in the Thổ dialect of Làng Lỡ (Nghệ An, Vietnam): an example of pitfalls for comparative linguistics. Quinzièmes Journées de Linguistique d'Asie Orientale, Paris, June 2001. HAL halshs-01128106.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Silent on stress. Gives the Làng Lỡ Thổ phoneme inventory and tone table (8 etymological tone categories, 1-6 on live syllables, 7-8 on stopped syllables, categories 5 and 6 merged; p. 4) and discusses spirants/hypercorrection. No mention of stress or accent.

sources.citation: Ferlus, Michel. 1996. Langues et peuples viet-muong. Mon-Khmer Studies 26: 7-28.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Scan without text layer; scanned (tesseract eng, 300 dpi). Ethnolinguistic survey of Vietic groups; §4.6 on the Thổ subgroup (Cuối, Làng Lỡ etc., p. 17) is ethnographic/historical. No statement on stress or accent; no phonological description of Cuoi.

sources.citation: Ferlus, Michel. 1994 [English version updated 2014]. Some peculiarities of Cuoi Cham, a Vietic language of Nghe-An (Vietnam). Neuvièmes Journées de Linguistique de l'Asie Orientale, Paris, 5-6 May 1994. HAL halshs-01079521.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Silent on stress. Historical-phonological notes on the Cuối Chăm variety (initials, registrogenesis, final *-l, vowels); says 'the Tho language varieties, including Cuoi, present full-fledged eight-tone systems' (p. 5). No mention of stress or accent.

sources.citation: Ferlus, Michel. 1994. Quelques particularités du cuôi cham, une langue viet-muong du Nghê-an (Vietnam). Neuvièmes Journées de Linguistique de l'Asie Orientale, Paris. HAL halshs-00927642.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: French original of the paper read in English translation; the English version (read) has no stress statement, so this is only a completeness check.
